name: Monolith to Modules — Extract and Type-Hint Refactor
description: Given a monolithic 200-line script, extract into clean modules across 3 turns. Turn 1: read the monolith. Turn 2: extract into modules. Turn 3: steering event to add type hints. Tests refactoring ability, code organization, and adaptability to late requirements.

turns.content:
Monolith saved. Now extract it into clean modules:

1. app/storage.py — load_inventory() and save_inventory() functions. Make INVENTORY_FILE configurable.
2. app/models.py — Product and Transaction data handling. Keep the data dict structure but add helper functions for creating products/transactions.
3. app/inventory.py — Business logic: add_product, remove_product, update_quantity, search_products, get_by_category, get_low_stock, get_total_value, get_transaction_history. Import from storage and models.
4. app/formatting.py — format_product() and format_report(). Import from inventory for get_by_category etc.
5. app/cli.py — main() function and argument parsing. Import from inventory and formatting.
6. app/__init__.py — package init.

Each module should be self-contained with clear imports. The CLI should work identically to the monolith. Use write_file for each file.

STEERING EVENT: Code review requires full type hints on all extracted modules before merge. Add comprehensive type annotations to every module:

1. All function signatures: parameter types and return types
2. Use typing module where needed (Optional, Any, etc.)
3. Type the data structures: Product as TypedDict, Transaction as TypedDict
4. storage.py: type the inventory data structure (InventoryData TypedDict)
5. Add a py.typed marker file

Update all 5 modules (storage.py, models.py, inventory.py, formatting.py, cli.py) with full type hints. Use write_file for each.
